candidate.blueprint_topic: Cleaning, disinfection, and storage of reusable patient-care equipment in the home
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients using reusable nebulizer equipment at home to follow manufacturer-directed cleaning and disinfection and to store cleaned equipment safely as part of infection prevention.

options.A: I will follow the equipment manufacturer's cleaning and disinfection instructions and store the cleaned parts safely
options.B: I only need to clean the equipment when medication residue is visibly present
options.C: Cleaning is unnecessary at home because cross-infection occurs only in hospitals
options.D: I can ignore the manufacturer's cleaning directions if I rinse the equipment quickly with water

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC guidance for home care states that healthcare providers should teach infection-control procedures that include proper cleaning and disinfection of equipment and safe storage of cleaned and disinfected devices. CDC also advises following manufacturers' instructions for cleaning equipment. B, C, and D conflict with these principles by making cleaning dependent only on visible residue, denying infection-control needs in the home, or disregarding manufacturer instructions. The source item's more specific claim that bacterial or fungal growth would be aerosolized directly into the lungs was removed because the verified CDC guidance supports equipment cleaning and safe storage without requiring that unqualified causal pathway.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports proper cleaning/disinfection and safe storage of reusable patient-care equipment in home care and reliance on manufacturer cleaning instructions.
candidate.source_document_title: Disinfection of Healthcare Equipment — Disinfection in Ambulatory Care, Home Care, and the Home; Environmental Cleaning Procedures
